text:
alex: dropping an nsys timeline from a long repro run — looks like an H2D memcpy on stream 3 is serializing kernels on stream 1. attaching capture id: /mnt/traces/capture_1734567890.qdrep

maria: can you paste the waterfall snapshot or the nsys export?

ken: is this the small-batcher path that does per-request KV prefetch? sounds like the prefetch triggers a hostcopy then kernel launch waits.

alex: yes — batcher=small-coalesce, path is kvcache->staging->H2D(stream3)->kernel(stream1). nsys shows memcpy ~3.2ms, kernel starts ~4ms after memcpy end. CPU thread shows a scheduling gap ~8-12ms between those NVTX markers.

lia: could be pinned allocation fallback — if the staging buffer isn't pinned, cudaMemcpyAsync can block and fall back to sync path on host.

maria: did we register the buffer with cudaHostRegister or use our pinned-pool? if not, it becomes pageable and driver does sync copy.

alex: command I ran: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --output out_1734567890 ./run_inference_bench --capture-id=1734567890``` captured full job + worker threads and NVTX around prefetch/execute.

perf-bot: auto-summary: H2D memcpy 3.2ms on cudaStream_3, kernel (conv) launch on cudaStream_1 delayed; overlap=0%. CPU worker-thread-47 had scheduling gap 9.1ms between nvtx:prefetch_end and nvtx:kernel_launch.

ken: that matches previous perfetto runs where copy engine contention + CPU preemption both showed up. if worker is preempted after issuing memcpy but before kernel launch we see this hole.

maria: two hypotheses: 1) staging buffer is pageable -> sync copy; 2) worker thread got preempted (low priority) before submitting kernel, so copy completed but kernel launch delayed. both possible simultaneously.

lia: quick mitigation idea: 1) ensure pinned-pool allocations for prefetch buffers; 2) mark cudaStreamNonBlocking and launch kernel on separate dedicated stream to avoid implicit sync on default stream; 3) bump prefetch thread niceness / use sched_setscheduler for that thread.

alex: agreed. plan to reproduce smaller: 1) microbench script that does only prefetch of XKB per request with k=1..8, 2) toggle pinned-pool on/off, 3) toggle thread priority. I'll attach the microbench commands.

ken: can you share the repro shell? I can run it on a few GPU SKUs.

alex: repro snippet: ```#!/bin/bash
# microbench prefetch-only
for i in 1 2 4 8; do
  ./kvcache_prefetch_bench --items $i --size 65536 --use-pinned=$1 --stream=3 --nvtx
done
```

maria: also try enabling cudaHostAlloc and do cudaMemcpyAsync from host pinned memory to see true overlap. if overlap shows up, problem was pageable staging.

lia: I'll flip the small-coalesce heuristic to try merging up to 4 KV lookups into one batched prefetch (reduce number of H2D ops). patch will be small.

ken: I'll run nsys against both versions and compare per-token latency and waterfall. I suspect larger batches will reduce relative overhead but can increase latency tail in some cases.

perf-bot: scheduled job perf-run-789 for repro on dev-gpu-2 at 1734571000. metrics to collect: H2D latency, kernel start offset, CPU preempt count, nvtx durations.

alex: assign: lia = change batcher heuristic, ken = run nsys microbench and attach captures, maria = verify pinned-pool + hostalloc test. target: EOD.

lia: on it :thumbsup:

ken: will run and upload captures here.

perf-bot: note: if you want less noise in nsys, add --sample=none and filter process by PID.

maria: one more note — also check memcpy size pattern. small many copies are worse than fewer larger ones due to DMA engine setup cost. try coalescing contiguous keys into one buffer.

alex: good call. may also try prefetch batching window of 10ms to allow coalescing across requests. we'll see tradeoffs.

ken: ok launching first set now. will post capture ids.

alex: thanks team — let's reconvene after earliest captures.
